evidence: All five judge.toml files and scoring.toml were parsed with tomllib and compared with the frozen template; no structural defect found. (1) tests/scoring.toml: `[gates] render = 0.0 / constraints = 0.0`, `[weights] functional = 0.6 / polish = 0.2 / visual = 0.2` (sum 1.0), `[floors] functional = 0.05`; LF-normalised bytes equal the template scoring.toml; each listed name has its directory in the right suite (tests/gates/{render,constraints}, tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual}). (2) Every [judge] block has exactly judge="claude-code", mode="batched", timeout, isolated=false, prompt_template="prompt.md" and no model/reasoning_effort/temperature/weight key; each [judge] block, including mcp_servers and the timeouts 600/600/9000/900/900, equals the template's. (3) Browser MCP: all five declare `name = "playwright"`, `command = "playwright-mcp"`, `args = ["--headless", "--isolated", "--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium", "--no-sandbox"]`. (4) Restart server: only tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:14-18 declares `name = "verifier"`, `command = "/usr/local/bin/python3"`, `args = ["/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py", "$APP_RESTART_HELPER"]`; tests/test.sh exports `export APP_RESTART_HELPER="$LOG_DIR/app-restart.sh"` after chmod 755 and before run_suite; test.sh, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py, Dockerfile and .dockerignore are equal to the template after LF normalisation. restart_mcp.py exposes the single tool `restart_app`; exactly one criterion (cw_save_reload_restart, functional judge.toml:339) names it and the functional prompt's `## Restart evidence` section names `the restart_app tool of the verifier MCP server`; the other four prompts say `Never restart the app.` (5) Aggregation: gates `all_pass`, scored `weighted_mean`. (6) Criteria: render 1, constraints 2, functional 43, polish 6, visual 3; ids unique within each file and across all files; id equals name everywhere; gate criteria all `type = "binary"`; functional and polish all binary; visual all `type = "likert"`, `points = 5` with anchors 5..0; all weights positive (functional 1.0/1.5/2.0 summing 59.0, others 1.0); every description non-empty; no unexpected criterion keys. (7) Prompts resolve: each prompt.md exists, contains exactly one `{criteria}` and one `{app_context}`, no other brace placeholder, and `http://localhost:3000`; tests/app_context.md contains no brace placeholder that could be mis-substituted. (8) Budget nesting: gates 600+600 < 1500, scored 9000+900+900 = 10800 < 11100, 1500+11100 = 12600 < [verifier].timeout_sec 13200.0. Counterexample attempts: a dead app cannot gain from wiring because gates are all_pass binary at weight 0.0 ahead of scored suites; a conforming app is not penalised by wiring because restart is offered only where the one criterion needs it and the helper relaunches with the same DB_PATH/entry as the first launch. Run evidence: no configured judge run exists for these bytes. The hosted run on the earlier candidate (verifier directory contains app-restart.sh and app-restart.sh.used; the restart criterion reasoning records a completed restart; all five dimensions returned scores) shows this same template wiring launching, resolving prompts and invoking the verifier MCP server, but it is not a measurement of these bytes. The private check-rubric-schema.py and check-scoring-policy.py were not executed; their documented behaviour was applied by hand. Notes: (a) the functional suite has 43 binary criteria in one batched judge call with a single-use restart tool, so a judge that calls restart_app out of order would spend it; this is template design and prompt-guarded, outside this row's structural scope. (b) the frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx and the skill's assets/WebDev_Rubrics_QC.xlsx have different file hashes; row 24 was read from the former (Quality and Internal sheets). (c) the Internal sheet's row 24 still speaks of reward.toml and a pinned judge, i.e. the retired layout; the shipped Quality Checks wording and skill reference were applied.
